question_type: two-cell lookup (same column, two FY-end rows) + under-specified finance formula ('implied Macaulay style duration' from two prices)
decisive_step: Not a data step: every cell and the reference retrieved the same two cells (Table 1 'Status of the Account of the Treasurer of the United States', column 'Total operating balance', FY1953 and FY1954 rows; first printed treasury_bulletin_1957_12.txt:1090-1091, unchanged through 1962_07; reference worklog Steps 5-6, review.md check 2-3). The decisive step is the FORMULA reading. The reference chose the reciprocal of the continuous log-yield (worklog Step 8, calc.py, confidence 'low') and was graded wrong. Cells a and b chose the trivial reading 'a zero maturing at the second observation has duration = one period' (a[20], b[25]); their value is within 0.1% of the key (error_bin within_0.1pct, which excludes numerically-equal) but not strict-equal. Cell c chose a two-cash-flow weighted-average-time reading (c[14]-[15]) and is >25% off. So the intended formula produces a value numerically almost identical to the trivial unit-period answer yet not string-equal under strict grading.

a.path_summary: find_tables on the question nouns returned the Status-of-the-Account table as the header match (a[5]); show_table --long --grep for each FY row printed both cells with the column identity check (a[7], a[9]); printings on both cells showed one value across every printing 1957_12..1962_07 with the 1959_06 OCR outlier flagged (a[11], a[12]). It then spent four long THINK blocks on the formula (a[13], a[16], a[18], a[20]), enumerated seven candidate expressions in one calc (a[17]), and settled on the trivial 'duration = the one elapsed period' reading, confirmed by a second calc (a[21]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Chose the reading in which the two balances only fix the yield and the Macaulay duration of a zero observed one period apart is the elapsed period itself, independent of the data.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell or the reference got it right. The reference chose a non-trivial reading (reciprocal of the log-yield, worklog Step 8) and was also wrong; the key sits within 0.1% of a's value, so the intended reading is a near-trivial variant nobody produced.

smallest_change.change: No adapter change is justified. All cells found and verified the right two cells with the tools in <=6 steps; the loss is the question's under-specified formula, on which the stronger reference solver also failed (confidence 'low', three readings listed in solution.json). The error bins show a and b's trivial reading is within 0.1% of the key but not equal, so the intended formula is a near-trivial variant that even a text sentence fixing the convention ('for a zero observed one period apart the Macaulay duration is the elapsed period') would reproduce as strict-wrong.
